thread:
Evan: heads up — finance wants a fast estimate of GPU hours change if we roll out the new price slab next month. they think some customers will shift to higher qps, others will throttle. need a quick read on second-order effects (kv cache hit rate, batching impact, and cross-region routing). :eyes:
Laura: can you sketch the scenario? is this the slab that reduces per-token price after 1M tokens/day?
Evan: yep. pricing team calling it `price_slab_v2` — thresholds: 0-1M tokens/day (base), 1M-5M (mid), >5M (discounted). their hypothesis: pro users will push into mid slab to save cost, which could increase sustained QPS and reduce prefix cache reuse per request.
Sanchit: quick thought: more sustained QPS = larger KV cache working set if sessions are sticky. that can drop hit rate ~5-12% depending on shard locality. if hit rate drops, per-token GPU compute rises.
Clarissa: do we have a recent baseline for KV hit rate vs concurrent sessions?
Laura: baseline (last 30d, eu-na steady): avg kv_hit = 78%, p95 qps = 420, avg seq_len = 120, gpu_hours/day = 3,200.
Evan: finance asked for 3 scenarios: conservative, expected, aggressive. can infra run an estimate of delta gpu_hours and cost impact for each? include routing fallback to lower-cost region if latency SLO allows.
Infra-bot: running simulation: `sim/gpu_impact --slab price_slab_v2 --windows 30 --regions eu,na` — ETA ~2m.
Infra-bot: simulation complete. results (summary): conservative: +4% gpu_hours, expected: +11% gpu_hours, aggressive: +24% gpu_hours. kv_hit delta conservative:-3pp, expected:-8pp, aggressive:-15pp. routing shift potential: up to 9% traffic rerouted to cheaper region without SLO breach.
Sanchit: that aligns with my back-of-envelope. aggressive assumes many clients shard by user id causing cache fragmentation. mid-case has more clients batching which helps amortize token cost but not enough to offset cache loss.
Clarissa: can we translate +11% gpu_hours into absolute hours and estimated monthly cost? also add headroom needed for autoscaler ramp (30m warm start for some GPU types).
Laura: using current, +11% => ~3520 gpu_hours/day (~3200 * 1.11). monthly delta ~ (320 extra gpu_hours/day * 30) = 9600 gpu_hours.
Evan: cost side: use internal gcloud list price mapping? rough price $3.1/gpu_hour for spot-equivalent, $5.6/gpu_hour for on-demand (example).
Sanchit: quick calc: 9600 * $3.1 = $29.8k (spot), or * $5.6 = $53.8k (on-demand). note: quantization and batching optimizations could cut effective cost by ~12% if enabled.
Evan: thanks. two follow-ups: (1) how much pre-warming headroom do we need for safe rollouts (k8s buffer)? (2) which routes to prefer for fallback to keep latency <100ms p95 for pro tier?
Infra-bot: pre-warm recommendation: maintain 12% spare capacity as buffer for first 3 days of rollout, then evaluate. For our clusters that maps to ~384 gpu_hours/day reserved (12% of expected 3200).
Laura: routing recommendation: prefer eu-west-1 as primary for EU customers, allow up-to-9% spill to na-west-2 if latency delta <25ms and SLOs still met. set policy: `route.policy: prefer_local_then_cost_with_latency_threshold=25ms`
Clarissa: we should add a KV cache instrumentation spike during beta to validate hit rates. small ask: add a synthetic workload run with 1.5x session churn to measure real-world delta.
Evan: agree. action items: - infra: run synthetic churn test and post logs in this thread (Sanchit) - eng-sre: prepare autoscaler cooldown tweak for rollout (Laura) - finance: prepare provisional headroom budget (Evan)
Sanchit: starting synthetic next hour, will log `synthetic/price_slab_v2/churn-1.5x` and share results.
Laura: I'll update rollout runbook with 12% buffer and routing policy.
Clarissa: tagging product/pm for communication to customers about quota nudges.
Evan: perfect. if we see >20% gpu_hours delta in the first 48h we rollback. :thumbsup:
Infra-bot: note added to thread metadata: simulation_id=sim-1765432100-01, artifacts: /sims/1765432100/summary.csv
Evan: thanks everyone — keep the short updates in thread.
